# Deployment Guide

This guide explains how to deploy the collector service on a small cluster. It assumes that you have installed the command line tools, created an account, and confirmed that the network policy allows outbound traffic to the registry. Read the whole document before you change anything in production.

## Before you begin

Confirm that the operator has a valid account, that the storage class exists, and that the image pull secret is present in the namespace. If any of these items is missing, create it and rerun the validation script. The script prints a summary of the checks and exits with a non zero status when a check fails. Keep the output of the script, because the support team asks for it whenever an installation fails.

Review the values file and set the replica count to a number that matches the size of the cluster. A small cluster usually runs three replicas, while a large cluster runs at least six. Do not set the replica count to zero unless you intend to stop the service, because the rollout controller treats zero as a request to remove every pod.

## Installation

Clone the repository into a working directory. Apply the manifests with the command shown in the quick start section. Watch the rollout until every pod reports ready. If a pod restarts more than twice, read the logs of the previous container and look for a missing secret or a mistyped host name.

The collector writes its state to the volume that the storage class provides. Back up that volume before you upgrade, and restore it if the new version refuses to start. The upgrade procedure keeps the old pods running until the new ones pass their health check, so a failed upgrade does not interrupt traffic.

## Licensing

Some of the bundled components are distributed under the following terms:

THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THE WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE AND NONINFRINGEMENT. IN NO EVENT SHALL THE AUTHORS OR COPYRIGHT HOLDERS BE LIABLE FOR ANY CLAIM, DAMAGES OR OTHER LIABILITY, WHETHER IN AN ACTION OF CONTRACT, TORT OR OTHERWISE, ARISING FROM, OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THE SOFTWARE OR THE USE OR OTHER DEALINGS IN THE SOFTWARE.

Ship the notice with every copy that you distribute, and keep the text of the notice unchanged.

## Troubleshooting

When the collector reports that the queue is full, raise the queue limit in the values file and restart the deployment. When the collector reports that the certificate has expired, renew the certificate and copy it into the namespace. When the collector reports that the disk is full, remove old snapshots and lower the retention period. If none of these steps helps, open a ticket and attach the output of the validation script together with the logs of the failing pod.

## Removing the service

Delete the manifests in the reverse order, then delete the namespace. The volume is not deleted automatically, so remove it by hand when you no longer need the data. Check the billing page afterwards, because some cloud providers keep charging for a volume that still exists.
